newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Budvar sell-off plans to go ahead - AgMin.
newsitem.headline: Czech Budvar sell-off plans to go ahead - AgMin.

text.p: The much-delayed privatisation of Czech brewer Budejovicky Budvar n.p. should go ahead as planned regardless of a continuing trademark dispute with Anheuser Busch Cos, the Agriculture Ministry said on Thursday.

Last week the ministry said it would present proposals to the government for the privatisation of Budvar, makers of Czech Budweiser beer, via a management buyout after lengthy talks with Anheuser Busch collapsed last year.
But the plans have already run into high-level opposition.

Roman Ceska, the chairman of the state privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF), was quoted in Czech newspapers on Thursday as saying that a management buyout was ill-conceived and that the trademark dispute should be solved before a sell-off could go ahead.

"Mr Ceska undoubtedly has the right to his point of view...the NPF isn't part of the decision making process it is here to execute decisions which have been made," the head of the ministry's privatisation department, Jiri Stehlik said.
"This form of privatisation is the least risky...Of course it is possible (to go ahead without solving the trade mark dispute)," he added.

The Czech government has delayed privatisation of Budvar while trying to settle a trademark dispute with Anheuser Busch, maker of the U.S. Budweiser, which has been battling with its small Czech cousin for most of the century.
The negotiations over the use of the "Budweiser" and "Bud" trademarks were aimed at resolving a row which prohibits the rivals from selling their labels in each other's key markets.

The Agriculture Ministry's plans, which allow for management eventually to gain majority control, are in line with the government's desire to privatise the makers of one of the country's most famous exports but to keep it primarily in Czech hands.
But the NPF boss said that the plan, under which a 10 percent stake in Budvar would be sold to management with an option for them to buy a further 41 percent later, was flawed.
"This model very often leads to the majority shareholder abusing his position and taking profits at the expense of other shareholders," Ceska was quoted by CTK news agency as saying.

Budvar is one of the five largest Czech breweries and "Budweiser" beer has been brewed for centuries in the southern Czech city of Ceske Budejovice known also by the German name Budweis, but the trademark was not registered by the Czechs until late last century.

The trademark conflict with Anheuser-Busch, which was founded by German immigrants to the United States, began in 1911 when the American brewery first insisted that it had registered the brand name before the Czechs.
